claim: P93 MEASUREMENT: with the part-name-normalization preserve class and the new compliance stage in place, python-xlsx reads 841/841 preserve-compatible over the 846-file corpus, and the compliance stage — pointed at real artifacts for the first time — finds 29 workbooks whose active edit ships two shared string tables. Not a gate: it records the water level the new instruments actually measure.

framework_changes.effect: preserve_partial_unexplained 54 -> 0. All 54 were source packages spelling parts with backslash separators or a lower-cased [content_types].xml; python-xlsx writing the canonical OPC name is a repair, and there was no compatibility class for it. python-xlsx preserve is 841/841, not 93.6%.

The shared rule registry now scans every roundtrip output, with source findings subtracted so only introduced defects count. Preserve cannot see this class: it compares output to input, so a package broken the same way on both sides passes 7/7. That is precisely how the P91 P0 survived preserve and passive roundtrip and surfaced only as a chance IndexError on reopen.
UTF-16 XML parts no longer crash a scan (16 files); part lookup is case- and separator-insensitive per OPC (removed 3 false positives); new rule part_name_case_unique.

open_items.symptom: Active edit output contains both xl/sharedstrings.xml (the source table, e.g. 38 entries) and xl/sharedStrings.xml (a fresh table holding only the newly written string). Reported as part_name_case_unique plus 408 shared_string_index_in_range findings.
open_items.root_cause: SharedStrings.flush() looks the part up by its canonical name only. OPC compares part names case-insensitively, so a package already carrying the lower-cased spelling is treated as having no shared string table and a second one is created.
open_items.impact: Silent data corruption. A reader resolving the new part sees every existing index rebound to a different string. Preserve passes 7/7 and the reopen check passes; only the compliance stage names it.
open_items.repro: spreadJS/1111.xlsx — open, write any string cell, save, list the archive.

open_items.symptom: AttributeError: 'Chartsheet' object has no attribute 'flush' during save.
open_items.note: Regression against the P92 measurement (active 840 -> 833). The chartsheet type dispatch added after P92 plugs the API leak but the new type does not implement the save-time protocol.

open_items.symptom: KeyError: "'ARIMA Module' has no worksheet part (empty r:id); it is a placeholder sheet". Was the P92 open item; now a typed error rather than a bare KeyError on ''.
BadZipFile — legacy OLE2 .xls content with an .xlsx extension. Documented substrate boundary.

next_gate: P94 requires compliance_introduced == 0 with xlsx-duplicate-sst-part-different-case closed and a regression test that opens a workbook whose sst part is spelled xl/sharedstrings.xml, writes a string cell, saves, and asserts the archive holds exactly one shared string part. active_roundtrip_pass_rate must also return to >= 99.8 with the chartsheet save path implemented.
notes: Compliance counts only findings absent from the source package; every number above is attributable to the library. The docx and pptx corpora have not yet been re-run under the compliance stage — 10-file smoke runs of each are clean.
